question: In 2020 researchers showed people COVID death charts on ordinary or logarithmic axes. What did the log charts do?
options: Helped people read the trend better
Made people understand it less well
answer: Made people understand it less well. In Romano and colleagues' survey experiment, log charts left people with a worse grasp of how the pandemic had grown, worse predictions and even different policy views. A log axis turns steady growth into a straight line, which only helps readers who know how to read it.
move: A chart helps only readers who know how its axis counts.
ask: Which chart have I shared that most readers could not decode?
trap: Assuming the expert's chart helps everyone who reads it.
source: Romano et al., the effect of logarithmic scale on COVID-19 charts, Health Economics, 2020
quote: when we show the number of COVID‐19 related deaths on a logarithmic scale, people have a less accurate understanding of how the pandemic has developed, make less accurate predictions on its evolution, and have different policy preferences
